## Zone 1 — fix the example, ⛔ NOT the registry

The card names the fork and I am ruling the scope, not the contract:

> The obvious fix is to lowercase the four `type` values… Worth deciding separately whether the registry should normalise case at lookup — that is a contract question… Recommend fixing the example; file the registry-normalisation question on its own if it is wanted.

**Your card is the example.** Lowercase `Page` / `Card` / `Text` / `Button` to the registered `page` / `card` / `text` / `button`.

⛔ Do **not** add `toLowerCase` (or any normalisation) to `packages/core/src/registry/`. That would make `Page` and `page` the same key **everywhere, for every component, permanently** — a contract change affecting every registered type, decided off one broken example. If you finish the example fix and think case-insensitive lookup is right, **say so in your report** and I will file it as its own decision card. Do not implement it.

## Premise — verify, and note the grep that misleads

The card's reasoning is sound and I have no correction to it, but verify on the tree rather than trusting either of us:

- `examples/hello-world/schema.json` uses PascalCase for all four node types.
- The registered spellings are lowercase, present in `packages/cli/src/utils/known-schema-types.ts` (derived from the registration calls themselves, per #5115).
- `packages/core/src/registry/Registry.ts` resolves through plain `Map.get` with no `toLowerCase` anywhere in that directory, so lookup is case-sensitive and every node falls through to the OBJUI-001 "Unknown component type" panel.

**Independent corroboration you can run**: `objectui check` already reports `Unknown schema type "Page" in examples/hello-world/schema.json`. It is one of only **two** real ObjectUI schema files in the whole repo the command warns about — buried until now under 45 false positives from `package.json`, which is #5127's defect, not this one.

Note this file is also `App.tsx`'s direct input (`import schema from './schema.json'`), so the render path is real, not hypothetical.

## Why this is worth a dev at all

It is the **smallest example in the repo — the one a newcomer opens first** — and it renders four error panels instead of a hello-world. Same failure shape as the closed #4061, where `objectui init` scaffolded an app with an empty registry so every node rendered "Unknown component type". That one was fixed at the scaffold; this is the committed example that still does it.

## Tests

Check whether `examples/hello-world` has any test harness at all before inventing one. If there is a natural home, pin that the example's node types are all registered keys — a check that reads the registry rather than restating the four strings, so the pin survives a rename. **If there is no harness, do not build one for this**: say so in the report, and rely on `objectui check` over the repo emitting no `hello-world` warning as the observable outcome. ⛔ Do not stand up test infrastructure for an example as a rider on a four-token fix.

Either way, report the before/after of:

```
node packages/cli/dist/cli.js check | grep hello-world
```

(`@object-ui/types` must be built before the CLI — `dist/cli.js` imports its `dist/zod/index.zod.js` at load.)

## Gates

Derive from your diff (`scripts/pm/dispatch-gates.mjs` is **objectstack-only**; here derive from `.github/workflows` + `package.json`). A changeset is likely **not** required — `examples/**` is not a published package — but run `check-changeset-presence.mjs` and report what it says rather than assuming either way.

⛔ **Do not background a long check and end your turn.**

## Deliver

Draft PR against `main`, first body line `Fixes #5236`. Return the JSON report and post it as a comment whose first line is the literal `<!-- os-dev-report -->` marker.

Cross-reference, posting the number now that it exists rather than leaving a forward reference: the registry-normalisation question is filed as **#5247** — *[Decision] Should component-registry lookup normalise case? Two measured instances of "every node renders Unknown component type"*, `needs-user-decision` with a four-prism block.

That is the card's own instruction executed (*"file the registry-normalisation question on its own if it is wanted"*), and the dev reached the same conclusion independently rather than implementing it — correctly, since it is a contract change for every registered type across the stack.

Two things I put in #5247 that are worth knowing here, because they cut against acting:

1. **Both measured instances are our own artifacts.** #4061 (the scaffold) and this card (the example) are things *we* wrote, each fixed at its source. That is measured **authoring** pull, not user pull — nobody should read "two instances" as evidence an outside author reached for PascalCase.
2. **My recommendation there is C, not B** — keep lookup strict, but make the failure teach (`Unknown component type 'Page' — did you mean 'page'?`). What both instances actually cost was not that the wrong spelling failed; it was that the failure said nothing about the cause. C fixes that without making a second spelling permanently valid, and note that B would also make `PAGE` and `pAge` resolve — a typo class, not just a naming convention.

This card (#5236) stays scoped to the example and closes on PR5244's merge.
